title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings, which can join Google Meet to participate in meetings
excerpt: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, allowing users to add Claude to video meetings as a visible participant so it can answer questions in real time during c
content_html:
Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, allowing users to add Claude to video meetings as a visible participant so it can answer questions in real time during calls, generate documents and whiteboards, and record meeting notes and to-dos, further expanding AI’s use in collaborative work scenarios.

During meetings, Claude replies in text by default and, once granted the appropriate permissions, can access connected tools to help organize information and handle tasks. After the meeting ends, the notes, records, and documents generated by Claude are saved together on a dedicated page on claude.ai for users to review and use later. On privacy, the system by default prevents Claude from joining meetings that include external participants to reduce the risk of unauthorized information access.

Currently, Claude Meetings is being tested with Team and Enterprise users and only supports Google Meet for now; Anthropic says it will expand to more meeting platforms in the future. In addition, organizations using HIPAA-compliant configurations or customer-managed encryption configurations cannot use the feature for now.

This update continues Anthropic’s product direction of building Claude into an all-in-one workplace tool. Previously, the company rolled out features such as whiteboards and data dashboards and continued to expand meeting notes and collaboration capabilities, pushing Claude to evolve from a conversational AI assistant into a work platform covering meetings, documents, and data processing.
